summary: Iteration 109 checked only the 62-day personal streak, using test-only isolated setups. Backend: 15/15 pytest tests passed through iso_harness (dedicated DB tejas_isolated_iter105_test, patched clock, synthetic X-Test-User auth, synthetic attempt docs). Frontend: tested on the preview URL. Playwright sent every /api/** request to a test-only bridge on 127.0.0.1:8765 (iso_bridge_streak_iter109.py), and each synthetic user had its own frozen IST clock. /api/auth/session returned a plain {user} object. Tested users: seven (7-day run, today completed), missed (best 8, current 0, two missed days, one day waiting for confirmation, one day in progress), full (62/62 after the series ended), pre (prelaunch), plus guest and an in-session user switch. All functional checks passed. Found 1 minor UI bug (dialog closing glitch) and a few minor design or reduced-motion gaps. No writes to the customer DB. Bridge stopped and test DB dropped.

minor.issue: Possible edge case, not reproduced (code review only): an active live attempt with deadline=0 (an untimed paper, rules.minutes=0) would always be classified 'pending' because the check is a['deadline'] <= timestamp. Live JEE papers are 180 min, so this is low risk. Suggest `a['deadline'] and a['deadline'] <= timestamp`.

Design note, not a bug: if yesterday's attempt is expired but not yet sealed, current_streak shows 0 until the student opens and seals it, even before midnight. The UI explains this with 'One last step: confirm your finish', so it is acceptable, but main may want to call out this behaviour.

ui_bugs.issue: On close, onClose sets selection=null straight away, so `{selection&&...}` empties the DialogContent while the Radix exit animation is still running. For about 150ms an empty 48px shell with only the X button is visible mid-screen. Measured: open height 421px, height while closing 48px, innerText 'Close'. Fix: keep the last selection in a ref/state until the dialog has fully closed, or render from a cached value.

issues: Several labels are 8-9px, which is hard to read: eyebrow 9px, track labels 8px, hero cup label 8px and small text 9px, cups-heading caption 9px, day-record summary caption 9px, mini card small 9-10px on mobile. Suggest at least 11px.
In prelaunch with no cups earned, the large hero cup is drawn in full gold under 'THE FINISH IS WORTH IT'. The label makes clear it is not earned, but a dimmed or locked style would remove any doubt.

prefers-reduced-motion suppresses all animations and transitions inside .streak-journey and .streak-dialog, and hides the confetti (verified: runner, cup and confetti off, fill transition 0s). But the DialogContent element itself still plays the shadcn 'enter' zoom/fade, and so does the overlay, because the rule only targets descendants (`.streak-dialog *`). The .streak-mini compact card's background transition is also not covered. Add `.streak-dialog,.streak-mini{animation:none!important;transition:none!important}` inside the media query.
When the current streak is 0 the card reads '0-day streak'. Something like 'Start a new streak' would read better.

backend: Prelaunch returns all zeros: 62 upcoming days, today_state null
First day; today grace keeps yesterday's streak until midnight IST; a missed yesterday breaks the run
7/15/30/45/62 consecutive runs earn exactly the matching cups, with earned_date = the day the run reached n
31 alternate-day finishes give total 31, best 1 and no cups
After a break the current run restarts; best and earned cups persist
Dec31→Jan1 run continues; Jan 29-31 run is preserved on Feb 1 and in March

Excluded: duplicate same-date attempt (deduped, earliest kept), practice, retry, preview, parent_attempt, other series_id, other user, non-completed status, submissions before 00:01 or after closes_at, out-of-range or malformed series_date, and submitted_at later than the clock
A sealed time_limit attempt counts; an expired active attempt shows as pending with an attempt_id and does not count until sealed; an active attempt with time left shows in_progress
Repeated GET writes nothing (collection snapshot unchanged); the response has no score, answer, key, marks or rank fields; each day has only {day,date,state,attempt_id}
frontend: Auto celebration (Bronze) shows once with 18 confetti pieces; localStorage key series-streak-seen:TEST_U_seven:all-india-jee-2026-27 = 7; no repeat after reload; a new user (missed) gets their own key and celebration; opening an earned cup manually replays confetti
A locked cup's dialog text is truthful and has no confetti
Runner and cup animations run; Pause motion sets animationPlayState=paused
Reduced motion: runner and cup animations none, confetti display none
Day record states (completed, missed, pending, in_progress, upcoming); result link /results/{id}; resume link /attempts/{id}; missed days have no link
Today action 'Confirm finish' opens the pending day
Simulated 500 shows streak-error, and Retry recovers
Guest sees the sign-in card (link /login?next=%2Fseries%2Fall-india-jee) with no API data; landing has no compact card
Login switch with a delayed (3s) streak response: the previous user's data never shows, the loading state shows
Compact card on /home links to the hub #my-streak
No horizontal overflow at 1920x800 or 390x844 (element-level check)

critical_code_review_comments: series_streak.py: the logic is pure and derived from data; read-only aggregation with $limit; _id excluded. Looks good.
SeriesStreak.js (65 lines): dense single-line JSX is hard to maintain; consider splitting into components or files.
Celebration effect writes to localStorage before setSelection. If the dialog is dismissed by navigating away, the cup is still marked as seen. Acceptable.
seed_data_creation: Synthetic attempt docs only, in tejas_isolated_iter105_test, which was dropped after the run. Customer DB untouched (0 TEST_U_ streak docs verified).
test_credentials: Synthetic x-test-user users only (TEST_U_seven/missed/full/pre). No real login.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_iter109_series_streak_isolated.py -p no:asyncio -n0 -v. The response is enveloped as {data:...}; series_id is all-india-jee-2026-27. Frontend bridge: cd /app/backend/tests && python iso_bridge_streak_iter109.py & (port 8765). It reads x-test-user to pick a per-user clock. In Playwright, intercept **/api/**, answer /api/auth/session with plain {user}, answer /api/auth/phone with a plain user object, and forward everything else to 127.0.0.1:8765 with the x-test-user header. No papers are seeded, so the banner shows 'starts 1 Dec' (harness artifact). finalize() uses Mongo $$NOW (real time), so genuine time_limit seals inside the harness get a 2026-01 submitted_at; use synthetic sealed docs instead. Afterwards, kill the bridge and drop tejas_isolated_iter105_test.
